# tests/fixtures/ — throwaway real-infrastructure harnesses a probe composes around its checks

## Files

- `harness.py` — the check runner: records PASS/FAIL, returns the process exit code. Open it while writing a probe's body, or when deciding what its exit code has to mean.
- `live_infra.py` — the reachability gate that reports a dead dependency as BLOCKED instead of a failure. Open it before the first check of any probe that needs Postgres, Valkey, or Vault.
- `probe_user.py` — a throwaway user identity: contextvar set on entry, data directory removed on exit. Open it for filesystem and contextvar paths.
- `residue.py` — the raising witnesses for a probe's own blast radius. Open it when your probe writes user files or Valkey keys.
- `scratch_db.py` — a throwaway Postgres carrying the shipped schema and the ownership bootstrap. Open it when a probe needs a real database rather than a fixture of one.

## Wiring

- Schema apply: `scratch_database` → `_apply_schema` → `_psql_file` twice, `_SCHEMA` then `_BOOTSTRAP`. That is the installers' order. Reversed, the bootstrap's `schema_migrations` table is already a public BASE TABLE when the schema's `$schema_precondition$` runs, so the apply stops with `requires an empty target database` and `_psql_file` raises carrying psql's stderr — loud at the apply. The ordering still matters for the skipped case: a bootstrap that never runs leaves every schema object owned by the superuser who applied it, and the next applier's step DDL then runs as the wrong role. Counterpart: `deploy/AGENTS.md`.
- Embedding values: `_embedding_args` → `clients/embeddings_provider.py:describe_for_installer(["describe", "local"])`. It is the entry `deploy/lib/embedding_config.sh:resolve_embedding_schema_args` also drives, and the fixture reads the same `<model> <dimensions>` output shape, so a return-shape change breaks the installer and this fixture in the same commit. Counterpart: `deploy/lib/AGENTS.md`, `clients/AGENTS.md`.
- Role provisioning: `_provision_roles` creates `_ROLES` when absent — the names in `deploy/postgresql.sh:ROLE_SQL`, minus passwords, `BYPASSRLS` on `mira_admin`. A renamed or re-privileged role on either side fails the fixture's schema apply. Counterpart: `deploy/AGENTS.md`.
- Identity: `probe_user` and `cleanup` call `utils/user_context.py`'s sanctioned set/clear pair, and nothing here touches the contextvar directly. The same two files also hardcode `<repo>/data/users/<id>`, a copy of the layout `utils/userdata_manager.py:base_dir` and `auth/provisioning.py:DATA_USERS_ROOT` build, so a move on the production side leaves `cleanup`'s `rmtree(ignore_errors=True)` deleting nothing while `residue.assert_user_removed` checks a path that never exists — the witness passes with the probe's debris still on disk. Counterpart: `utils/AGENTS.md`, `auth/AGENTS.md`.
- pgvector pointer: `_require_pgvector`'s error names `docs/MANUAL_INSTALL.md`, and `docs/AGENTS.md` carries the same-commit obligation on that pointer — a message reworded away from the guide path edits the guide's entry in the same commit. Counterpart: `docs/AGENTS.md`.
- Probe shape: `require` → enter `scratch_database` / `probe_user` → checks → exit the block → `residue` witnesses → `finish()`. A witness called inside the block sees pre-teardown state and passes while the debris is still there; `finish()` called before teardown prints a PASS for a probe that then leaves residue behind.

## Rules

- Import a fixture by module name after putting `<repo>/tests/fixtures` on `sys.path` — `from harness import check, finish`. No `__init__.py` exists anywhere under `tests/`, so `import tests.fixtures.harness` works only by namespace-package accident when the repo root happens to be on the path. Copying a fixture into `/tmp` forks the scaffold: the copy keeps passing after the original is fixed, and the probe certifies the stale twin.
- `require` goes before the first `check`, never inside one. `live_infra.require` prints its own `<SERVICE>-PROBE-BLOCKED` line and calls `sys.exit(3)`, so a `require` inside a check does report the block — but it ends the process before `finish()` prints `SUMMARY`, so every remaining check is silently dropped and the run's record cannot tell a mid-probe block from a probe that died at startup.
- No fixture transcribes the apply's artifacts: `_SCHEMA` is the shipped schema file and `_embedding_args` asks the installer's own `describe_for_installer`, so a production-side change reaches the fixture with no edit — a transcribed copy would pass while production is broken, which makes the probe certify the copy. Three literal lists do stand: `live_infra._PORTS` hardcodes 5432/6379/8200, so a moved port reports BLOCKED on a service that is up; the users root and `_ROLES`'s role names carry their consequences under `## Wiring` above.
- `probe_user`'s teardown is best-effort — `cleanup` runs `shutil.rmtree(..., ignore_errors=True)` and `probe_user` discards the returned bool — so a failed removal raises nothing. `residue.assert_user_removed` after the block is the only thing turning that into a signal; without it the debris survives and fails the next probe's residue check for damage that probe did not cause.
- Keep a fixture's import side-effect free. `probe_user` and `scratch_db` reach project code only inside the call, after putting `_REPO` on `sys.path`; an eager project import drags `clients/__init__.py`'s import chain (embeddings, Postgres, SQLite, Valkey, Vault) into fixture import, so the gate breaks on a half-broken tree and hides which layer failed.
- `residue.py` witnesses two surfaces — the user data directory and a Valkey key prefix. Nothing witnesses a leaked scratch database, so a probe killed between `CREATE DATABASE` and the `finally` leaves a `mira_probe_*` in place with no error anywhere; check `pg_database` by hand after an interrupted run.
- A probe connected with `scratch_database`'s `**conn_kwargs` is a superuser, so RLS does not apply — the schema's policies are written `TO mira_dbuser` only. Witness RLS by reconnecting as `mira_dbuser` with no `app.current_user_id` set and asserting zero rows and no error; the same assertion made on the admin connection passes while RLS is broken.

Elsewhere: this map does not own the doctrine that decides when a probe is the right artifact, nor the craft of writing one — those bind every probe in the repo, so they live at their own authority instead of being restated per directory. Admission and the permanent batteries are `tests/protected/AGENTS.md`; probe anatomy and the disposable-probe pattern are the out-of-tree `writing-probes` skill; who reaches these fixtures is a grep — `rg 'tests/fixtures'` hits maps, notes, and the fixtures' own docstring citations. Every other destination this directory reaches is an edge — see `## Wiring` above.
